source.title: Junior School Curriculum Design - Integrated Science - Grade 9 (First published 2024, ISBN 978-9914-52-946-3)
source.notes: Fetched via WebFetch, which saved the PDF locally; WebFetch's own summarizer could not extract text ('raw PDF binary stream'), so per the known workaround the Read tool was used directly on the locally-saved PDF path, which parsed the full text natively. All strand/sub-strand headings, specific learning outcomes, and key inquiry questions below were read verbatim from the document text, not summarized by an intermediate model. Title match: the mirror's filename ('integrated-science-grade-9-july-2024-1-unlocked') matches the confirmed official KICD Google Drive filename 'Integrated Science Grade 9 - July 2024.pdf' recorded in this repo's README. The document's own cover/title page does not print a month, only 'First published 2024' and ISBN 978-9914-52-946-3, but the mirror filename and content (Junior School Grade 9 Integrated Science) are consistent with the confirmed official title, so this is treated as the authentic document, not a look-alike or older version. IMPORTANT FINDING: the app's existing curriculum.ts strands for Integrated Science ('Living Things & Environment', 'Matter, Force & Motion', 'Energy', 'Earth & Space' - 4 strands) do NOT match the real design, which has only 3 strands ('Mixtures, Elements, and Compounds', 'Living Things and their Environment', 'Force and Energy') and no 'Earth & Space' strand at all (no solar system / weather systems / environmental management content in this design). This needs to be flagged and corrected before any Integrated Science skills are audited or built.

subStrands.name: Structure of the atom
specificLearningOutcomes: Describe the structure of the atom
Determine the mass number of elements
Draw the electron arrangement in atoms using dot or cross diagrams
Classify elements into metals and non-metals
Show interest in classifying elements into metals and non-metals
keyInquiryQuestions: How is the structure of the atom important?
subStrands.notes: Suggested 14 lessons. Content covers: structure of the atom (protons, electrons, neutrons); atomic number and mass number of elements; electron arrangement of elements; energy level diagrams (cross or dot); metals and non-metals. Explicit scope note in source: use only the first 20 elements of the periodic table; do NOT introduce the periodic table itself at this level.

subStrands.name: Metals and Alloys
specificLearningOutcomes: Describe the physical properties of metals
Describe the composition of alloys
Identify the uses of metals and alloys in day-to-day life
Explain the effects of rusting of metals
Appreciate the importance of common alloys in day-to-day life
keyInquiryQuestions: How are alloys important in day-to-day life?
subStrands.notes: Suggested 16 lessons. Content covers: physical properties of metals (state, ductility, malleability, electrical and thermal conductivity); composition of alloys (steel, stainless steel, bronze, brass, duralumin); uses of metals and alloys in day-to-day life (sodium, magnesium, aluminium, copper, iron, gold, silver, brass, steel, bronze, duralumin, stainless steel); rusting (causes, effects, prevention).

subStrands.name: Water hardness
specificLearningOutcomes: Describe the physical properties of water
Distinguish between hard and soft water in nature
Apply methods of softening hard water in day-to-day life
Outline the advantages and disadvantages of hard and soft water
Appreciate the applications of soft and hard water in day-to-day life
keyInquiryQuestions: What is the importance of different types of water?
Why is hard water preferred for drinking?
subStrands.notes: Suggested 14 lessons. Content covers: physical properties of water (taste, colour, odour, boiling point); hard and soft water; methods of softening temporary hard water (boiling, addition of washing soda, distilling) - explicit scope note: avoid ion exchange; advantages and disadvantages of hard water and soft water.

subStrands.name: Nutrition in Plants
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify external and internal parts of a leaf
Explain adaptations of the leaf to photosynthesis
Describe the process of photosynthesis
Investigate the conditions necessary for photosynthesis
Appreciate the process of photosynthesis in nature
keyInquiryQuestions: What is the importance of photosynthesis in nature?
subStrands.notes: Suggested 18 lessons. Content covers: parts of a leaf (external and internal); adaptations of the leaf to photosynthesis; structure of chloroplasts (membranes, grana, stroma); process of photosynthesis - explicit scope note: chemical reactions during light and dark stages are not required; conditions necessary for photosynthesis.

subStrands.name: Nutrition in animals
specificLearningOutcomes: Outline modes of nutrition in animals
Describe the structure and functions of different types of teeth
Classify animals based on their dentition
Describe the process of digestion in human beings
Appreciate that animals have varied modes of nutrition
keyInquiryQuestions: How is food digested in the human body?
subStrands.notes: Suggested 16 lessons. Content covers: modes of nutrition in animals (parasitic, saprophytic, symbiosis, holozoic); dentition in animals (homodont and heterodont; carnivorous, herbivorous, omnivorous); types of teeth (incisors, canines, premolars, molars) - structure and functions; process of digestion in human beings (ingestion, digestion, absorption, assimilation, egestion).

subStrands.name: Reproduction in plants
specificLearningOutcomes: Outline functions of parts of a flower
Describe pollination in plants
Outline the adaptations of flowers to wind and insect pollination
Explain fertilisation and fruit formation in flowering plants
Categorise fruits and seeds based on their mode of dispersal
Recognise the role of flowers in nature
keyInquiryQuestions: How does reproduction in plants occur?
subStrands.notes: Suggested 20 lessons. Content covers: functions of parts of a flower; meaning and types of pollination (explicit scope note: details on factors that promote/hinder self-pollination not required); adaptations of flowers to wind and insect pollination; fertilisation, seed and fruit formation in flowering plants (explicit scope note: details of double fertilisation not required); fruit and seed dispersal in plants (modes and importance).

subStrands.name: The Interdependence of Life
specificLearningOutcomes: Explain the biotic and abiotic factors of the environment
Construct food chains and food webs in the environment
Describe the effect of human activities on the environment
Appreciate the interdependence between living and non-living factors of the environment
keyInquiryQuestions: What is the role of living and non-living factors in environments?
subStrands.notes: Suggested 18 lessons. Content covers: biotic (living) components of the environment (predation, parasitism, symbiosis, competition, saprophytic); abiotic (non-living) components of the environment (temperature, light, water, wind, atmospheric pressure, pH and salinity); energy flow in an ecosystem (food chains and food webs); effect of human activities on the environment (habitat change, hunting and poaching, introduction of new living things). Explicit scope note: avoid details of chemical reactions and specific microorganisms involved in nitrogen, carbon and sulphur cycles when discussing decomposers.

subStrands.name: Curved mirrors
specificLearningOutcomes: Describe types of curved mirrors
Draw ray diagrams to locate images formed by concave and convex mirrors
Describe the characteristics of images formed by concave and convex mirrors
Explain the uses of concave and convex mirrors in day-to-day life
Appreciate the applications of curved mirrors in day-to-day life
keyInquiryQuestions: How are curved mirrors used in day-to-day life?
subStrands.notes: Suggested 18 lessons. Content covers: types of curved mirrors (concave, convex, parabolic surfaces); image formed by concave and convex mirrors (locating images, characteristics of images across object positions: at infinity, beyond C, at C, between C & F, at F, between F and P); applications of curved mirrors in day-to-day life (solar concentrators, car headlamps, shaving mirrors, dentists' mirrors, projector lamps, telescopes, supermarket mirrors, driving mirrors).

subStrands.name: Waves
specificLearningOutcomes: Describe the generation of waves in nature
Classify waves as longitudinal and transverse
Describe basic characteristics of waves in nature
Describe remote sensing in relation to waves
Describe applications of waves in day-to-day life
Appreciate the applications of waves in day-to-day life
keyInquiryQuestions: How are waves applied in our day-to-day life?
subStrands.notes: Suggested 16 lessons. Content covers: generation of waves; classification of waves as longitudinal and transverse; characteristics of waves (parts of a wave - amplitude, wavelength, frequency, period, wave speed, phase; wave equation velocity = wavelength x frequency; straight line motion, reflection, bending of waves, movement around objects); remote sensing (reflection, absorption, transmission of electromagnetic radiation at different wavelengths; active/passive remote sensing; remote sensing platforms); applications of waves in day-to-day life (medical - ultrasound, X-rays, CT scans, MRI scans, cancer therapy, laser surgery; communication - radar, radio, cell phone, television, Wi-Fi, operation of drones; cooking - microwave).
